At the first Congress meeting of the year he moved that non-professional personal services be excluded from campaign spending limits; the motion was referred to the Rules and Elections Committee, and he said the clarification would prevent future controversies, having been disqualified the previous year in his bid for ASG president on a spending technicality. The 1973 Talisman counts the Academic Council members and alternates as part of the roll of Congress.

note: Elected with 350 votes. She said that if being an officer meant only building a float it was not a job worth having, and that two people could not represent an entire class; she favoured a student government made up solely of college representatives.

src.label: Herald 53:52, 12 Apr 1974, 'Election results'; 1975 Talisman, Classes (Sophomores), p. 394

name: Jay Keffer
note: The 1975 Talisman says Keffer and his vice-president held the only two freshman seats on the student government, and that both thought the inclusion of class officers in student government essential. He had contested the top freshman post with Jack Harris in the autumn election.

name: Tom Hayes
note: Ran on making the dorms more like home. The first of his reforms, passed by ASG in November 1974, provided a method by which residents could obtain change for vending machines, which resident assistants had not been allowed to give out. He suggested increasing the number of class officers while restricting voting rights to the president and vice-president.

name: Steve Henry

note: A Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter page says Steve Henry and Stan McDivitt were elected as members of the Associated Student Government that year. He had lost the presidency to Jeff Consolo by 797 votes to 767 in April 1974 and won it the following year.

name: Evie Shrewsbury

name: Hank Miles
note: Named with Evie Shrewsbury in the same caption of graduates conferring at an ASG meeting. A Hank Miles had been alternate Academic Council representative for Applied Arts and Health in 1972-73.

name: Mary Pat Swift
note: An Alpha Xi Delta chapter page names her as one of four sisters who were representatives for the Associated Student Government. She stood for representative-at-large in April 1974 and finished twelfth with 396 votes in a race where ten were chosen, so if she sat it was by later appointment or through a vacancy; the archive records two seats filled by presidential appointment in February 1975 after Christy Vogt resigned. Recorded because a source states the membership, with the conflict shown.
